And B moved from columns 33–41 to columns 36–44: 3 to the right.
Hmm! So LEFT moved A 3 to the left and B 3 to the right. But RIGHT moved A 9 to the right and B 3 to the left. Asymmetric!

So RIGHT: A +3 (right), B −3 (left). LEFT: A −3, B +3. So the arrow keys move A in the direction of the key, and B in the opposite direction! A and B move in opposite directions: RIGHT pushes A right and B left (they move away from each other... no wait, A is on the left side, B is on the right side. A right = toward B; B left = toward A. So RIGHT brings A and B closer together (toward the central stripe). LEFT separates them.
Hmm interesting. Or: the keys move the "pair" symmetrically? RIGHT: A right, B left = both toward the center. LEFT: A left, B right = both away from the center.
So the light-blue stripe in the middle is a fixed divider, and A and B slide toward/away from it. The movement is 3 cells per key press (the width of the stripe?).
So the game is: A (the 7 with the dots) and B (the L) slide horizontally toward/away from the central stripe. C (the yellow L) is fixed.
What's the goal? Probably to make A and B touch/overlap? Or to align A's dots with something? Or to move A and B vertically too (UP/DOWN) to fit A into C's position?
Hmm, wait. Maybe the goal is: to make A and B combine into a complete shape? A is a "7" (top bar + right tail), B is an L (top bar + left tail). If A and B are adjacent... A's shape: 3x9 bar + tail on the right. B: 3x9 bar + tail on the left. If placed side by side... hmm.
Or maybe the goal is to rotate A (SPACE/ACTION7) to make it an L, and then fit it into C's slot? But C is fixed at rows 45–53, columns 51–59.
